headline: Dolores Huerta died at 96. She coined "Sí, se puede."
summary: Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California. She was 96. She was a teacher in the San Joaquin Valley who quit because her students came to class hungry, and went to organize farm workers with César Chavez. Their union became United Farm Workers. She was jailed 22 times and got the Medal of Freedom in 2012.
cover_answer: Yes, it can be done. It became a union's rallying cry.
table_question: Would you keep a secret for decades to protect something you built?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A woman named Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday. She was 96, as old as a great-great-grandmother. She spent her whole life helping the people who pick our fruit and vegetables get treated fairly, and her saying was "Sí, se puede," which means "Yes, it can be done." She lived a long, full life, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if it comes up. One long life, one saying they can repeat.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them a saying to repeat and the people who pick the fruit on their plate, then stops. This age fears what it can picture, so 96 is a great-great-grandmother, not you. Expect "are you going to die?" Not for a long time.

8-12.script: Dolores Huerta was a teacher whose students came to class hungry. She quit to organize the people picking the crops, with César Chavez, and their union joined a grape strike that ran five years. A union is the whole class refusing to play until the rule is fair: one picker can be replaced, hundreds can't.
8-12.why: Hungry students, a union, a five-year strike. The chain is her life.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether rules are fair, so the script runs her life as one chain: hungry students, a union, a five-year strike. The class refusing to play says why one picker alone could not have done it. Expect "did they win?" Yes. Contracts with the big growers won benefits for the fields.

13-17.script: Would you keep a secret for decades to protect your life's work? Dolores Huerta built the United Farm Workers beside César Chavez. This year she said he raped her in those early years, and she stayed quiet for the movement. Second: does "Sí, se puede" belong to her, or to him?
13-17.why: The work, and what it cost her. Let them say which weighs more.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the union she built changed farm workers' lives, and the man she built it with raped her, a secret she kept to protect it. The script asks who the slogan belongs to, and they are testing whether you argue it honestly. Expect "was she right to stay quiet?" She said she had to protect the movement.

5-7.q: Why did she go to jail 22 times?
5-7.a: For marching with the farm workers. It wasn't for doing something bad. She kept going anyway.

8-12.a: Yes, it can be done. Obama said he stole it for his campaign.
Everyone stops work until the boss agrees a fair deal.

13-17.q: Why did she wait so long to tell?
13-17.a: To protect the movement, she said. Sooner? "I don't know."

13-17.q: Does this change what Chavez did?
13-17.a: The union stands and so does the harm. Say where you land.
